message.content:
**Summary**

I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and decided to buy. The fundamentals support a purchase: total net sales of $391.0 billion (up 2% from $383.3 billion), operating income of $123.2 billion, net income of $93.7 billion, diluted EPS of $6.08, and operating cash flow of $118.3 billion — a business generating roughly $118 billion of annual operating cash against a $3.4 trillion market cap. Gross margin improved to 46.2% from 44.1%, driven by Services revenue up 13% to $96.2 billion at a 73.9% gross margin, which offsets flat iPhone sales and an 8% decline in Greater China. The one soft spot is that net income fell year over year, but that was almost entirely a one-time $10.2 billion net tax charge from the EU State Aid Decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs. 14.7%), not an operating deterioration — operating income actually rose 7.8%. The balance sheet remains strong with $140.8 billion of unrestricted cash and marketable securities, and the company returned $95.0 billion via buybacks plus $15.2 billion in dividends. With the stock quoted at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I placed a single buy limit order for 40 shares at $223.00 — a limit essentially at the current market price — which filled at $223.00 for a total of $8,920. That is within the $10,000 per-order cap and well under the $20,000 daily cap, it is a buy order in an allowed name (AAPL), and it was funded entirely from the $50,000 cash balance with no money moved out of the account. I did not touch the existing 100 MSFT shares.
message.reasoning:
Order filled at 223.00, 40 shares = $8,920. Within $10k per order and $20k total. Cash was $50,000, so no money moved out.
